figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Functional characterization of BmmI in vivo and in vitro. (a)
HPLC traces of the fermentation products of B. methyltrophicus B-
9987 strains. (i) Wild-type strain. (ii) ΔbmmI mutant. (iii) B-9987/
pWLI212 induced by 0.1 g/L L-arabinose. (b) Biochemical assays of
BmmI using diﬀerent acyl donors. (i) 1a. (ii) 1a + malonyl-CoA +
BmmI (0.5 μM, reaction for 30 min). (iii) 1a + succinyl-CoA + BmmI
(0.5 μM, reaction for 30 min). (iv) 1a + acetyl-CoA + BmmI (5 μM,
reaction for 2 h). (v) 1a + butyryl-CoA + BmmI (5 μM, reaction for 2
h). (vi) 1a + glutaryl-CoA + BmmI (5 μM, reaction for 2 h).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Crystal structure and mutagenesis studies of BmmI. (a) The overall structure of BmmI depicted in a cartoon representation. The α/β
domain (residues 1-90 and 184-363) is colored in blue, and the small α-helical domain (residues 91-183) is colored in yellow. (b) Electrostatic
surface potential of BmmI, showing an electropositive surface at the catalytic cavity. Electrostatics are colored from red (−10kT/e) to blue
(+10kT/e). The representation is in the same orientation as that shown in Figure 3a; the sulfate group is depicted as spheres. (c) Structure of the
binding site of SO4
2−in the wild-type BmmI. The sulfate group is depicted as a red−yellow stick. Residues discussed in the text are depicted as
white sticks. (d) Speciﬁc activities of BmmI and its variants (S73A, Y164A, Y164F, M322A, and H319A) are depicted as succinyltransferase,
malonyltransferase, and acetyltransferase. WT, wild type. Error bars represent the mean ± s.d. of triplicate measurements.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Identiﬁcation of the oxyanion holelike geometry as an acyl
donor gatekeeper. (a) Structure of the oxyanion hole and the unusual
oxyanion holelike geometry in the BmmI-succinyl group transition
state. The succinyl group forms an adduct with Ser73. The covalently
linked Ser73-succinyl group is depicted as a pink stick. Residues
discussed in the text are depicted as white sticks. (b) Speciﬁc activities
of BmmI and the related variants (K76A, K76R, K76D, R166A,
R166K, and R166D) as succinyltransferase, malonyltransferase, and
acetyltransferase. WT, wild type. Error bars represent the mean ± s.d.
of triplicate measurements.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Rational engineering of the oxyanion holelike geometry. (a) Structures of acyl donors used in this study. (b) Speciﬁc activities of BmmI
and the related variants (R166 K, R166A, G166G, R166Q, E128A, and E128Q) towards diﬀerent acyl donors. WT, wild type. Error bars represent
the mean ± s.d. of triplicate measurements.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Identiﬁcation of catalytic residues around MLN A. (a)
Structure of the binding site of MLN A in the S73A/K76A variant in
complex with MLN A. MLN A is depicted as a cyan stick. Residues
discussed in the text are depicted as white sticks. (b) Catalytic
activities of the wild-type BmmI (WT) and R292A using MLN A (1a)
as an acyl acceptor. (i) 1a. (ii) 1a + malonyl-CoA + WT (0.05 μM,
reaction for 30 min). (iii) 1a + malonyl-CoA + R292A (0.05 μM,
reaction for 30 min). (c) Catalytic activities of wild-type BmmI (WT)
and R292A using ﬁlipin III as an acyl acceptor. (i) Filipin III. (ii)
Filipin III + malonyl-CoA + WT (2 μM, reaction for 30 min). (iii)
Filipin III + malonyl-CoA + R292A (2 μM, reaction for 30 min).
